**Crystal Palace (home) vs AFC Bournemouth, Premier League (2024/25 season, Gameweek 33), scheduled for April 19, 2025, 3pm at Selhurst Park.**[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)

This preview relies exclusively on information available before April 19, 2025. The match was a home game for Palace against a Bournemouth side chasing European spots. They sat 12th in the table, five points behind Brighton in 10th and 11 behind Aston Villa in seventh, with European qualification slipping away. However, they were strong at home, with five consecutive home wins across all competitions and goals scored in their last 12 home games (since a 2-0 loss to Fulham in November 2024).[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)
- **Bournemouth**: Ended a five-game winless run (six in the Premier League) with a 1-0 home win over Fulham on or around April 14, 2025, via an early Antoine Semenyo goal. They were 8th in the table, six points behind Chelsea and Aston Villa, still with a slim chance at the top seven/Europe. They had scored a league-high 32 goals away from home that season (second only to Liverpool’s 40).[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)

### Injuries and Suspensions
**Palace** (pre-match): Long-term absentees Chadi Riad and Cheick Doucoure (both knee). No fresh injuries from the Newcastle defeat. Adam Wharton was a candidate to return to the starting XI; Daichi Kamada and Eddie Nketiah were options in attack.[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)

**Bournemouth** (pre-match): Luis Sinisterra (thigh) ruled out; Justin Kluivert (knock) had a chance of featuring after missing the Fulham game. Ryan Christie (groin) and Enes Unal (knee) were long-term absentees. Marcos Senesi was substituted at half-time against Fulham (tactical, on a yellow card).[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)

### Venue, Travel, Fatigue, and Other Factors
- **Venue/Home Advantage**: Selhurst Park (Crystal Palace’s home). Palace had a strong recent home record, including scoring in 12 straight home games. Bournemouth, however, were prolific on the road.[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)
- **Travel/Fatigue**: Short distance between Bournemouth and London (roughly 100 miles/2 hours by road). Palace faced potential midweek fatigue after the heavy 5-0 loss at Newcastle.[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)
- **Crowd/Home Atmosphere**: Standard Premier League home advantage expected for Palace at Selhurst Park; no specific anomalies noted in previews. - **Other Storylines**: Bournemouth were pushing for a European finish and had momentum from their recent win. Palace were looking to bounce back from consecutive heavy defeats and stabilize at home. No major pitch, altitude, or weather issues were highlighted in available previews.[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)

Pre-match predictions in sources leaned toward a competitive game, with one suggesting a narrow Bournemouth win (1-2) due to their away scoring form and Palace’s fatigue, though Palace’s home strength was acknowledged as a counter-factor.[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)[[1]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/crystal-palace/preview/crystal-palace-vs-bournemouth-prediction-team-news-lineups_570468.html)

Sources for the above include dated previews and stats pages from April 17, 2025, and earlier (e.g., Sports Mole, Squawka, Premier League sites, and historical H2H databases). All details predate April 19, 2025.

analysis.reasoning: While Crystal Palace boasts a strong recent home record, including five consecutive home wins and scoring in 12 straight home games, several factors significantly diminish this advantage. Palace is coming off a 'heavy 5-0 loss at Newcastle' and 'consecutive heavy defeats', indicating poor overall form, coupled with 'potential midweek fatigue'. Conversely, Bournemouth possesses an exceptionally strong away attack, having scored a league-high 32 goals on the road. They also carry recent momentum, having broken a five-game winless streak with a victory, and have a clear motivational drive, chasing European spots. Although Bournemouth has some attacking injury concerns, their formidable away scoring record suggests they can still pose a substantial threat. The net effect of Palace's poor overall form and fatigue against Bournemouth's strong away attacking prowess and recent momentum leads to an adjustment favoring Bournemouth.
